entities.name: Keratsa of Bulgaria
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Keratsa of Bulgaria (Keratsa-Maria; c. 1348–after 1390) was a Bulgarian princess who became Byzantine empress consort as wife of Andronikos IV Palaiologos. Her marriage tied the Shishmanid Bulgarian court to the embattled Palaiologan dynasty during the empire's late fourteenth-century crises—civil wars, Ottoman advance, and Genoese–Venetian entanglement.

As empress she stood at the centre of Andronikos IV's contested reign and usurpation politics against John V, when Constantinople's ruling family split under external pressure. Bulgarian dynastic brides were diplomatic instruments in Balkan balance-of-power strategies.

Keratsa's life illustrates how late Byzantine empresses embodied interstate alliance in a shrinking Christian Balkan world.
